question.text: Which of the following correctly describes DALYs averted as a social-impact metric?

answer.text: Disability-Adjusted Life Years averted — a non-monetary health impact metric combining mortality and morbidity reductions
Discounted Annual Lifetime Yields — a monetary return metric
Direct Annual Livelihood Yield — a livelihood metric
Daily Active Loan Users — a microfinance metric

explanation.text: **The Logic:** DALYs averted = Disability-Adjusted Life Years averted, a WHO-standard non-monetary health metric combining years of life lost (mortality) and years lived with disability (morbidity). Used in SAS-200 healthcare assessments. **The Trap:** The acronym DALY is specific to health economics; options B/C/D invent plausible-sounding expansions. **Cross-Exam Context:** DALY is used in WHO Global Burden of Disease studies and is commonly cited in health-sector impact work. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When certifying DALY-based claims, require (i) the baseline mortality/morbidity rate source, (ii) the disability weight used (usually WHO), and (iii) the geographic scope. Vague DALY numbers without these three anchors should be qualified in the SIR.
